topics.title: HTML Basics
topics.content:
HTML (HyperText Markup Language) is the structure of the web. Use tags like <h1>, <p>, <a>, <img> and <div> to structure content. Example: <h1>Hello</h1>.

Block-level elements create sections, inline elements appear inside lines of text.

quiz.question: Which tag is used for the top-level heading?
quiz.explanation: The <h1> tag denotes the top-level heading in an HTML document.

quiz.question: Which tag creates a hyperlink?
quiz.explanation: The <a> tag with the href attribute creates a hyperlink.

topics.title: Forms & Inputs
topics.content: Forms collect user input. Use <form>, <input>, <label>, <button>, <select> and <textarea>. Always associate <label> with inputs using the for/id attributes for accessibility.

quiz.question: Which attribute associates a label with an input?
quiz.explanation: The label's 'for' attribute should match the input's 'id' to associate them.

topics.title: CSS Basics
topics.content: CSS styles HTML. Use selectors and properties: p { color: blue; }. You can include CSS inline, in <style> tags or in external .css files.

quiz.question: How do you select an element with id 'main' in CSS?
quiz.explanation: Use the hash symbol: #main selects the element with id='main'.

topics.title: JS Basics
topics.content: JavaScript is the language of the web for behavior. Use const, let, functions, and DOM APIs like document.querySelector.

quiz.question: Which keyword declares a block-scoped variable?
quiz.explanation: Both let and const declare block-scoped variables; var is function-scoped.

quiz.question: Which method selects the first element that matches a CSS selector?
quiz.explanation: document.querySelector(selector) returns the first matching element.
